text:
Sofia R: heads-up — ACME is seeing a sudden spike of 429s starting ~03:12 UTC after we pushed the new rate limit policy. They say it affected both new and existing API keys. sample from their logs:
```
2026-02-17T03:12:07Z ERROR request failed status=429 path=/v1/generate token=sk-*** headers={"x-rw-rate-limit-remaining":"0", "x-rw-quota-reset":"1676626320"} body=\"{\"error\":\"quota_exceeded\"}\"
```
Sofia R: they've attached a repro curl as well (trimmed):
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-xl","input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Sofia R: they claim traffic is steady (no huge burst) — this looks like per-token quota enforcement kicked in fast after the config roll. tagging eng: @Kenji S and @Liam P for triage.

Kenji S: looking. which policy pushed? I see a config push at 03:10 by deploy pipeline: `rate-limit-config v3.4.0` that changed per-key burst window from 60s -> 30s and lowered burst tokens from 1500 -> 800 for the STANDARD plan. DeployBot left this in the deploy log: `DeployBot: rate-limit-config v3.4.0 canary=10% start=2026-02-17T03:10:00Z`.

Liam P: thanks. if canary was 10% we should only see subset affected — either policy routing mismatched or the canary tag didn't stick. Can we confirm the canary selector?

DeployBot: rate-limit-config v3.4.0 applied: selector=route:api-tier=standard, canary=10%, sticky=false, deploy_id=rlc-20260217-0310

Maya K: quick checks I ran:
- queried edge logs for deploy_id `rlc-20260217-0310` and see spikes of 429s across multiple shards (not just the canary).
- sample entry: `edge01 -> rlc-20260217-0310 route=api-tier=standard key=acct-3482 status=429 reason=quota_exhausted`
- but interestingly, some keys with `api-tier=enterprise` also show 429s (shouldn't be targeted).

Kenji S: possible causes: mis-evaluated selector (label mismatch), sticky=false causing config to propagate beyond intended nodes, or a bug in the routing lookup where untagged requests fallback to new policy.

Sofia R: ACME's billing contact says they were charged normally and didn't change anything on their side. They provided timestamps and ~2000 failed requests over 5m window.

Liam P: repro steps I want to run from our side: 1) curl with an account that should be in canary, 2) curl with an account that should be outside canary, check `x-rw-policy-id` and `x-rw-rate-limit-*` headers, and 3) verify per-route policy mapping in the configstore.

Kenji S: running 1&2 now from a sandbox agent. reproducer commands: 
```bash
# should be canary-candidate
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-canary-candidate" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# should be control
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-control" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Kenji S: results: both returned `x-rw-policy-id: rlc-20260217-0310` and remaining=0 after a few small requests. so the canary policy seems to be applied globally.

Maya K: rolling back looks safest — impact is broad and customer-affecting. options: 1) quick rollback of rate-limit-config to v3.3.9, 2) narrow selector and re-deploy v3.4.0, or 3) increase burst tokens to match previous behavior.

Liam P: rapid plan: rollback to v3.3.9 for now, monitor for 15m, then recreate canary with explicit tag + sticky=true. I can cut the rollback if we agree.

Sofia R: ACME needs immediate relief. they asked for ETA.

Oncall-Bot: paging @Liam P oncall (pager duty).

Liam P: I'm on it. initiating rollback now. will post commands.

DeployBot: command received: `/deploy rollback rate-limit-config --to v3.3.9 --reason "urgent rollback: global 429s"`

DeployBot: rollback started: rollback_id=rb-20260217-0322, executing across control-plane. Estimated finish ~90s.

Kenji S: watching edge logs. initial 429 rate dropping in the canary shard group.

Sofia R: pinged ACME at 03:24 UTC — they report failures dropping dramatically and new requests succeeding.

DeployBot: rollback completed: rollback_id=rb-20260217-0322 status=success finished=2026-02-17T03:25:14Z applied_version=v3.3.9

Maya K: confirmed headers from our repro now show `x-rw-policy-id: rlc-20260201-0310` (old policy) and `x-rw-rate-limit-remaining` is non-zero after small bursts.

Liam P: summary and next actions:
- rollback completed and mitigated customer impact (ACME confirmed).
- create an incident ticket (INC-20260217-42) with details and attach edge logs + deploy diff.
- root cause suspects: canary selector evaluation bug or sticky flag not honored during rolling deploy.
- postmortem owner: Kenji S. expected triage meeting tomorrow 10:00 PST.
- follow-up deployment plan: re-introduce v3.4.0 with `sticky=true`, explicit selector `route:api-tier=standard AND account_id IN canary_set`, canary=5%, and health check gating on 429 metrics.

Sofia R: I'll run customer comms and add notes to the incident. ACME asked for credit for the failed calls — I'll start a billing review with FinOps.

Kenji S: I pulled a short grep of the configstore diff:
```diff
- burst_window: 60
- burst_tokens: 1500
+ burst_window: 30
+ burst_tokens: 800
```
Kenji S: Also adding a quick check to the deploy pipeline to assert `canary==0` or `sticky==true` when selector is route-scoped. PR coming.

Maya K: good. I'll keep an eye on other customers on STANDARD tier for any residual blips.

Liam P: thanks everyone. I'll file the postmortem draft and link this thread. closing the immediate escalation.

Oncall-Bot: incident INC-20260217-42 created and assigned to Kenji S.

Sofia R: ACME replied: "Thanks! Service looks normal again. Appreciate the quick rollback and the follow-up." :thumbsup:

Kenji S: assigning follow-ups in jira, will add detailed repro steps + test harness for the selector logic.

Maya K: note for the postmortem — add a section on sanity checks for chained policy evaluation, and ensure deploy logs include the active selector snapshot.

Liam P: end.
